_readme: How a breaking change in this SDK is carried across to the bots that already call it.
One file, two consumers, and the same entries answer both:
- src/api-check/java/.../ApiRulesCheck.java, run by ci.yml and by ../release.sh, which treats an
entry as coverage for a break japicmp reports. A break named by nothing here fails the build --
'we forgot to write the migration' becomes red in the SDK repo rather than broken on a user's
machine weeks later.
- Studio's Upgrade SDK report, which shows 'summary' verbatim and applies 'fix' automatically.
This replaced a pair of files -- an OpenRewrite recipe YAML at META-INF/rewrite/ plus a prose-only
upgrade-notes.json. OpenRewrite existed to let a user migrate with `mvn rewrite:run` and no Studio;
once that stopped being a requirement, an engine we do not control bought nothing that Studio's own
rewriter (parser/refactor/CallMigrator) could not do, and cost a dependency on three OS installer
legs. The executable/prose split is now a FIELD, not a file.
== The shape ==
"schema":   1, required. See 'Evolving this file' below.
"versions": { "<version>": [ entry, ... ] }, keyed by the release that INTRODUCED the break.
Each entry:
"member":  what broke. Matched against japicmp's report and must be exact --
a type   -> com.botmaker.sdk.api.vision.ImageFinder
a member -> com.botmaker.sdk.api.vision.ImageFinder#find
a ctor   -> com.botmaker.sdk.api.Point#<init>
a field  -> com.botmaker.sdk.api.interaction.Key#ENTER   (enum constants included:
an enum constant IS a static field)
A trailing * globs, for the case where a whole package moved at once.
"summary": one sentence, always present, always shown to the user as written.
"fix":     the automatic repair -- see the kind table. EXACTLY ONE of fix/manual per entry.
"manual":  a sentence telling the user what to do, when no fix can express it.
== fix.kind ==
renameMethod       to                      Mouse.clickAt(..)   -> Mouse.click(..)
renameType         to (FQN)                a package move is the same kind
renameField        to                      constants and enum constants
moveMember         toType (FQN), to?       Tolerance#TIGHT -> Precision#TIGHT; methods too
dropArgument       index
reorderArguments   order  (e.g. [1, 0])
insertArgument     index, value, import?   value is source text: "Precision.TIGHT"
Optional "when": { "arity": 2 } scopes a fix to one overload. It is needed because call sites are
matched by ARITY, not by argument type -- Studio's scanner runs without bindings, on projects that
are half-edited and on no classpath it owns. Without 'when', a rename hits every overload.
Unmigratable BY CONSTRUCTION, so nobody hunts for the missing kind: a changed return type, an
instance<->static flip, and a member whose semantics changed while its signature did not. Those are
'manual' entries. If this file fills up with them faster than with fixes, the API is being changed
without regard for the people who have to run it.
== Upgrading across several releases is ORDERED REPLAY, not a chain ==
A bot on 1.x jumping straight to 3.0.0 gets every version in (from, to] applied as its OWN pass, in
ascending order, each running over the source the previous pass produced. So 2.0.0's foo->bar runs
first, and 3.0.0's bar->baz then finds 'bar' -- which is exactly what its 'member' names, because it
was written in 3.0.0's spelling. Entries never need to know about each other and nothing resolves a
chain.
Two rules keep that honest, and both are enforced in code:
- ONE pass per version, in order. Never iterate to a fixpoint: a->b in 2.0.0 and b->a in 3.0.0
would loop forever, where ordered replay correctly produces a no-op.
- The REPORT replays the names too. A 3.0.0 note about 'baz' has to be shown against a call site
the user's file still spells 'foo', so each pass keeps a rename trail and note matching resolves
through it. Without that, the most confusing upgrade there is -- renamed twice, then dropped --
reports a note about a name that appears nowhere in the project.
== Evolving this file ==
Three versions are in play, as everywhere else here: this file's schema, the Studio reading it, and
the checker. The checker lives in this repo beside the file and always understands it. STUDIO is the
one that lags -- a bot can pin an SDK newer than the Studio editing it.
- Adding a fix.kind does NOT bump 'schema'. An older Studio that meets an unknown kind degrades
that entry to manual (it still shows the summary) and disables auto-apply for the whole upgrade,
never silently skipping it. That graceful degradation is the entire point of having the rule.
- Bump 'schema' only for a grammar change that would make an older reader MISREAD an existing kind
-- the case degradation cannot cover. Studio refuses a file whose schema it does not know, whole,
and says so; it still reports breaks, which come from scanning the jar and need no file at all.
'versions' is empty because nothing has broken yet: the contract starts at v1.1.0 and v1.0.26 is the
last release that predates all of this.
